## TL;DR

This is slice 1 of #1080, as the owner re-scoped it on the board: acceptance criteria 1–3 only. It adds `review.freezeAfterPasses` (default 4, with a Settings control), a lighter blocking bar for P3 tasks and "Easter eggs bundle" tasks from pass 1, and an authoritative `## Accepted scope…` section that is quoted into the reviewer prompt. Criteria 4–7 and the new "Land anyway" override are slice 2, filed as #1081 and not implemented here. Tests pass and the scoped `repoos check` passed on the earlier version of this slice; I have not re-run it since the scope cut, so a fresh run is needed before review.

## Work and rationale

The owner's note says to ship slice 1 small and fast, so I kept it to the prompt, the parser and the config. I backed out the criterion 4 pieces I had already added: the enumeration closer, the "do not stop at the first instance" wording, the engineer self-review sentence and their tests. Those now belong to #1081.

- **One function picks the bar.** `reviewBlockingBar(task, config)` returns `full`, `light` or `frozen`. `frozen` wins over `light`, so a P3 task at pass 5 is frozen. The threshold reads `review.freezeAfterPasses` and falls back to 4, the same pattern `reviewHumanFlagThreshold` uses.
- **The bar is its own prompt section.** `blockingBarSection()` renders the bar and the accepted-scope quote after the landing checklist and before "How to inspect it", so the reviewer reads the bar before it hunts for bugs.
- **Accepted scope is read from the body.** `acceptedScopeSection()` takes the heading matching `^## Accepted scope` through the next `## ` heading, capped at 4000 characters. Subheadings stay inside the quote. The prompt quotes it verbatim and says the listed items and anything they supersede are not blocking.
- **The suggestions heading switches only when frozen.** Before the freeze the output asks for `## Suggestions`; after it, `## Suggestions (non-blocking)`. The section parser accepts both, so frozen reports still reach the suggestions field.

## Approaches tried

I first considered making the frozen heading the only heading. I rejected that, because existing reports and the UI read `## Suggestions` and migrating them would have been a larger change. Accepting both spellings in the parser is smaller.

I also considered quoting the accepted scope into the spec block. A separate section is easier to test against a fixture body and makes the reviewer treat it as authoritative rather than as more task text.

## Challenges and blockers

- The first scoped check ran in the background for a long time. Its earlier version of the slice passed with exit 0.
- The board copy of the task changed mid-run, which left the worktree copy stale. I read the current copy with `repoos show 1080` and followed the new slice boundary.
- Formatter rewraps made one scripted edit fail on its first match. It stopped before writing, so no partial edit landed.
- RepoOS made a WIP checkpoint commit (`5a2940f3a`) from my earlier work. That is bookkeeping, and the working tree holds only the slice-1 backout on top of it.

## Key learnings

- Keep the reviewer-visible text in one place. The closer line and the frozen heading both change what the parser reads, so each needs a test in the same change.
- A pure bar function, `f(task, config)`, makes the freeze testable without running a reviewer. The prompt wording is then the only thing that changes per pass.
- Housekeeping failures that waste rounds are out of scope and tracked elsewhere: #1076 (stray other-task bookkeeping in branches) and #1061 (bookkeeping commits invalidating checks).
